scenes.headline: What actually makes a looped transformer work
scenes.sub: IFM Research untangles Ouro from Huginn, one design axis at a time
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Crocus! Looped transformers reuse one block of layers many times. Two families, Ouro and Huginn, differ in three ways at once. Which one matters?

scenes.text: Isolate the three axes at matched depth, and two wires do almost all the work: an untied prelude and coda, and re-injecting the input every pass.
scenes.mark: two wires do almost all the work
scenes.say: Isolate the three at matched depth, and two wires do almost all the work: an untied prelude and coda, and re-showing the loop its input every pass.

steps.say: Huginn-style models first run tokens through a prelude of eight blocks. Ouro-style models skip it: the whole network is the loop.
Then a tied core of twelve blocks runs eight times, and a coda finishes. Both designs are matched at a hundred and twelve block executions.
A write gate re-injects the prelude's output into the core at every pass, not just once, through a learned per-channel gate.
And the loop's starting state is either the input itself, or random noise: the move borrowed from equilibrium models, and assumed to be essential.

scenes.title: From Ouro to Huginn, axis by axis

items.text: Start from a full-stack Ouro loop
items.say: Start from Ouro: twenty-eight blocks, looped four times.
Untie a prelude and coda, and multi-step reasoning jumps: twelve points on MATH500.
Re-inject the input every pass, and five benchmarks rise, though math reasoning drops.
Randomize the starting state, and it's close to a wash. The direct start wins six benchmarks of ten, and it's cheaper.

scenes.text: What a looped model does each pass matters more than how its state gets seeded.

recap: Untie a prelude and coda around the loop
Re-show the loop its input at every pass
Random state init is close to a wash
scenes.say: To recap: an untied envelope, the input at every pass, and no need for random noise. A first look, at small scale, with code still to come.
